_review: The Ember slice (2026-11-22; places from src/world/sow.js SOW_FARMS, SOW_SIGNS) (docs/phase-11/ember-design.md §9): Cole, the new steam, the six farms of the Sow.
title: The Mountain Is Waking

npcs.name: Cole
npcs.about: A miner's boy from Cinderhold. His father went into the deep tubes and did not come up. He ran down the mountain to warn anyone who would listen. No one has.

npcs.name: Aled
npcs.about: Keeps a flock on the high pasture above the valley. Has buried two wives and outlived the old mill.

npcs.name: Nia
npcs.about: Aled's granddaughter, nine. Talks to the sheep.

npcs.name: Bethan
npcs.about: A widow who runs the cistern farm with her son. Sells figs to the miners.

npcs.name: Tomos
npcs.about: Bethan's son. Carries the figs up to Cinderhold.

npcs.name: Huw
npcs.about: Threshes for the whole valley on the best floor in the Sow. Proud of it.

npcs.name: Elin
npcs.about: Huw's wife. Keeps the bees.

npcs.name: Ffion
npcs.about: Keeps hens and a dog that will not go into her byre.

npcs.name: Dai
npcs.about: Ffion's grandson. Ffion's dog follows him everywhere.

npcs.name: Gwil
npcs.about: Has the only well in the lower valley and has never let anyone forget it.

npcs.name: Sian
npcs.about: Gwil's daughter. Does the work her father talks about.

npcs.name: Mari
npcs.about: The oldest vines in the Sow are hers. Her grandmother planted the bottom terrace.

npcs.name: Rhys
npcs.about: Mari's son. Would rather be anywhere else, until someone says so.

npcs.name: Morcant
npcs.about: Head of the guild of Cinderhold. Knows where the tithe goes.

npcs.name: Teg
npcs.about: The guild's measurer. Reads the bell in the deep seam every morning and writes it down.

npcs.name: Vell
npcs.about: The guild's purse. Every debt in Cinderhold is in Vell's book.

npcs.name: Bron
npcs.about: Foreman of the deep shift. The miners do what Bron says, and Bron does what the guild says.

npcs.name: Nesta
npcs.about: Pushes the carts from the middle gallery. In debt to the guild for her mother’s burial.

npcs.name: Ifor
npcs.about: A miner of the rows. Owes Vell four seasons.

npcs.name: Gethin
npcs.about: Ifor's boy. Runs the lamps.

npcs.name: Annick
npcs.about: The Seer of the Ash Chapel. Has read the mountain for fifty years and been right every time.

npcs.name: Nerys
npcs.about: The eldest of the faithful. Knows the scripture by heart, and has never had to read the end of it.

npcs.name: Bryok
npcs.about: Keeps the cells. Came up the mountain twenty years ago to die and never did.

npcs.name: Lio
npcs.about: Rings the hours. Has not missed one in eleven years.

npcs.name: Elowen
npcs.about: Born at the chapel. Has never been below the scree.

npcs.name: Idris
npcs.about: Tends the spring. Has noticed. Has said nothing.

ember.cole.warn.speaker: ember-cole
lines: You're not from the mines. Are you from the north?
My father went into the deep tubes at Cinderhold and didn't come up. The guild says the tubes have always smoked. They haven't. Not like this.
There's steam on the north-west flank. New steam, where the old maps don't show any. The ground's waking up.
Nobody listens to me. Go and look. You'll see.

ember.cole.wait.speaker: ember-cole
lines: The north-west flank. High up, above the scree. You'll see it smoking if the wind's right.
Put your cold on it. Then tell me it's nothing.

ember.cole.seen.speaker: ember-cole
lines: You saw it. Then it's true.
The farms in the green valley west of the cone. The Sow. Six families. They sell us figs and laugh at the guild.
They won't believe the mountain. They believe their own ground. If something's wrong at a farm, they'll see it if you show them.

ember.cole.after.speaker: ember-cole
lines: I'm going back up for my father. Don't tell me not to.

ember.aled.hello.speaker: ember-aled
lines: You'll be the thing from the north. I heard. Nia, inside.
The flock's up on the high pasture. They came down to the fold this morning and wouldn't drink from the trough. Sheep are fools.
It always shakes in autumn. My father said so and his father.

ember.aled.mountain.speaker: ember-aled
lines: The mountain does what the mountain does. My sheep are my business, and they're fine.

ember.aled.show.speaker: ember-aled
lines: What is it?

options.text: Show him the trough by the fold.

ember.aled.shown.speaker: ember-aled
lines: Warm. The spring under the fold's run cold eighty years.
...They knew. The flock knew before I did.

ember.aled.waits.speaker: ember-aled
lines: I believe you. I won't be the first to run down that road with my tail up. Not while the others sit tight.

ember.aled.liar.speaker: ember-aled
lines: You told the Prys girl it went last night. It didn't. Go and tell someone else.

ember.aled.gone.speaker: ember-aled
lines: We're going. Go on, see to the others.

ember.aled.lied.speaker: ember-aled
lines: Tonight? ...Then we go now. Leave it all. Go!

ember.aled.stays.speaker: ember-aled
lines: No promise, no going. The flock and I will see what the mountain does.

ember.aled.ready.speaker: ember-aled
lines: The others are going. Then I'll go. But the flock can't walk the coast road in a day.
Will you come back for them? Say it and I'll go.

options.text: Promise to come back for the flock.

ember.nia.a.speaker: ember-nia
lines: Grandad says you're a ghost. Are you?

ember.nia.b.speaker: ember-nia
lines: We're going to the sea. I've never seen it.

ember.bethan.hello.speaker: ember-bethan
lines: We've nothing to spare, if that's what you're after. Tomos sold the last figs at Cinderhold.
The cistern's down by half overnight. Not a crack in the plaster I could find, and I looked.

ember.bethan.mountain.speaker: ember-bethan
lines: The mountain's the mountain's business. My cistern's mine.

ember.bethan.show.speaker: ember-bethan
lines: What is it?

options.text: Show her the crack at the old waterline.

ember.bethan.shown.speaker: ember-bethan
lines: There. I looked straight at that and didn't see it.
The ground's drinking it. Or cooking it off. All right. All right.

ember.bethan.waits.speaker: ember-bethan
lines: I'll go. I'm packing. Just give me a moment to think who else.

ember.bethan.liar.speaker: ember-bethan
lines: You lied to the others about the night. Why would I listen to you about my water?

ember.bethan.gone.speaker: ember-bethan
lines: We're going. Go on, see to the others.

ember.bethan.lied.speaker: ember-bethan
lines: Tonight? ...Then we go now. Leave it all. Go!

ember.bethan.stays.speaker: ember-bethan
lines: Someone stays with the harvest. Go.

ember.bethan.ready.speaker: ember-bethan
lines: We're ready. The figs are in the loft. Will you help us get them on the cart, or do we leave them?

options.text: Tell them to leave the harvest.

ember.tomos.a.speaker: ember-tomos
lines: Mam doesn't trust anyone from up the mountain. Or down it.

ember.tomos.b.speaker: ember-tomos
lines: I'll get the cart round.

ember.huw.hello.speaker: ember-huw
lines: Mind the floor. Best floor in the Sow. Every family threshes here.
It's been warm underfoot this week, mind. Elin says it's the sun. I say she's right, she usually is.

ember.huw.mountain.speaker: ember-huw
lines: Smoke on the mountain? There's always smoke on the mountain.

ember.huw.show.speaker: ember-huw
lines: What is it?

options.text: Show him the crack across the threshing floor.

ember.huw.shown.speaker: ember-huw
lines: That wasn't there at harvest. It's breathing. The floor's breathing.
My grandfather laid this floor. Elin. Elin, come and look.

ember.huw.waits.speaker: ember-huw
lines: I'll not be the first. If Bethan goes, I'll go. She's never been wrong about a thing.

ember.huw.liar.speaker: ember-huw
lines: They're saying you lied about the night. I've no time for liars.

ember.huw.gone.speaker: ember-huw
lines: We're going. Go on, see to the others.

ember.huw.lied.speaker: ember-huw
lines: Tonight? ...Then we go now. Leave it all. Go!

ember.huw.stays.speaker: ember-huw
lines: Someone stays with the harvest. Go.

ember.huw.ready.speaker: ember-huw
lines: Bethan's gone. Then we go. The grain's in sacks. Load it with us, or leave it?

options.text: Tell them to leave the harvest.

ember.elin.a.speaker: ember-elin
lines: Huw thinks the floor is the valley. He's not wrong.

ember.elin.b.speaker: ember-elin
lines: Thank you. He'd never have seen it on his own.

ember.ffion.hello.speaker: ember-ffion
lines: Don't mind the dog. He won't go in the byre. Hasn't for three days.
I lost four hens in there this week. Not a mark on them. Foxes, Dai says. Foxes don't leave the hen.

ember.ffion.mountain.speaker: ember-ffion
lines: The mountain? I've hens to see to.

ember.ffion.show.speaker: ember-ffion
lines: What is it?

options.text: Show her the byre, and what is on the floor.

ember.ffion.shown.speaker: ember-ffion
lines: The air. It's the air in there. The dog had more sense than me.
Dai. Get your coat. Don't go in the byre.

ember.ffion.waits.speaker: ember-ffion
lines: I'll go. I'll go now. Only, someone has to tell the others.

ember.ffion.liar.speaker: ember-ffion
lines: You told them it would go and it didn't. Dai believed you. Now he doesn't believe anyone.

ember.ffion.gone.speaker: ember-ffion
lines: We're going. Go on, see to the others.

ember.ffion.lied.speaker: ember-ffion
lines: Tonight? ...Then we go now. Leave it all. Go!

ember.ffion.stays.speaker: ember-ffion
lines: Someone stays with the harvest. Go.

ember.ffion.ready.speaker: ember-ffion
lines: The hens are in the basket. Help us with the rest, or go?

options.text: Tell them to leave the harvest.

ember.dai.a.speaker: ember-dai
lines: The dog won't go in there. I don't either.

ember.dai.b.speaker: ember-dai
lines: Are the hens coming too?

ember.gwil.hello.speaker: ember-gwil
lines: The only well below the terraces. Everyone comes to Gwil in a dry year.
Water's been sweet as ever. Bit warm. Sian says it tastes of eggs. Sian says a lot.

ember.gwil.mountain.speaker: ember-gwil
lines: You climbed the mountain and you come down here to tell me about it? I've a well to mind.

ember.gwil.show.speaker: ember-gwil
lines: What is it?

options.text: Draw the bucket in front of him.

ember.gwil.shown.speaker: ember-gwil
lines: Hot. The well's hot. Forty years and it's never been warm.
Sian was right. Don't tell her I said so.

ember.gwil.waits.speaker: ember-gwil
lines: I'll go when the others go. The well's the valley's. I can't leave it while there's a family drinking from it.

ember.gwil.liar.speaker: ember-gwil
lines: You lied to them. I knew you would. Off my land.

ember.gwil.gone.speaker: ember-gwil
lines: We're going. Go on, see to the others.

ember.gwil.lied.speaker: ember-gwil
lines: Tonight? ...Then we go now. Leave it all. Go!

ember.gwil.stays.speaker: ember-gwil
lines: Someone stays with the harvest. Go.

ember.gwil.ready.speaker: ember-gwil
lines: The others are on the road. The well's no one's now. Help us load, or do we go light?

options.text: Tell them to leave the harvest.

ember.sian.a.speaker: ember-sian
lines: The water tastes of eggs. I'm not making it up.

ember.sian.b.speaker: ember-sian
lines: He'll never say I was right. I'll take it anyway.

ember.mari.hello.speaker: ember-mari
lines: The bottom terrace is the oldest. My grandmother planted it.
The vines down there are going brown at the root. In autumn. It's not the season for it. Rhys says it's blight.

ember.mari.mountain.speaker: ember-mari
lines: The mountain was here before the vines. It'll be here after. That's not news.

ember.mari.show.speaker: ember-mari
lines: What is it?

options.text: Take her down to the bottom terrace.

ember.mari.shown.speaker: ember-mari
lines: The soil's warm. In my hand, it's warm.
It's not blight. Rhys, it's not blight.

ember.mari.waits.speaker: ember-mari
lines: I'll not leave the vines while the floor's still threshing. If Huw stays, the valley stays.

ember.mari.liar.speaker: ember-mari
lines: You lied. Huw's girl believed you and stood on the road all night. Go away.

ember.mari.gone.speaker: ember-mari
lines: We're going. Go on, see to the others.

ember.mari.lied.speaker: ember-mari
lines: Tonight? ...Then we go now. Leave it all. Go!

ember.mari.stays.speaker: ember-mari
lines: Someone stays with the harvest. Go.

ember.mari.ready.speaker: ember-mari
lines: Huw's gone. Then it's true for all of us. The wine's in the cellar. Help Rhys load it, or leave it?

options.text: Tell them to leave the harvest.

ember.rhys.a.speaker: ember-rhys
lines: Mam won't leave the vines. Nobody can make her.

ember.rhys.b.speaker: ember-rhys
lines: I'll stay for the vintage. Someone has to.

ember.orrin.hello.speaker: ember-orrin
lines: The mountain's grumbled since my grandfather held this chair. The guild decides what it means. Not a ghost from the north.
Three masters, three votes. Talk to Teg, if you like numbers. Talk to Vell, if you like money. You'll get no further with me.

ember.orrin.tithe.speaker: ember-orrin
lines: You've been at the shaft. I can see it on you.
The tithe keeps the seams open. It always has. Something below wants feeding, and we feed it, and we eat.
So. What will you do with what you saw?

options.text: Say you'll forget the cage, if the guild opens the lower tube to the coast.

ember.orrin.deal.speaker: ember-orrin
lines: Then we understand each other. The tube opens when the guild votes. My vote is yes.
And the cage goes down one last time. It's owed.

ember.orrin.after.speaker: ember-orrin
lines: The guild has voted. Go and tell someone else's village about the end of the world.

ember.orrin.sealed.speaker: ember-orrin
lines: You took my miners. The tube is shut. Whoever needs it can go round the mountain, in the fire.
Get out of my hall.

ember.teg.hello.speaker: ember-teg
lines: I read the bell in the north gallery every morning. Twenty years of mornings, in the book.
It's been reading warm. Warm is a word. I don't vote on words.

ember.teg.show.speaker: ember-teg
lines: You read the bell? Then you saw a number. What was it?

options.text: Show Teg the bell in the north gallery.

ember.teg.shown.speaker: ember-teg
lines: Past the last mark. Past the mark my master cut, and his master.
I'll vote to go. I'll say it in the hall with the number in my hand.

ember.teg.yes.speaker: ember-teg
lines: My vote is yes. One more, and the guild moves.

ember.vell.hello.speaker: ember-vell
lines: Every miner here owes the guild. If they walk away from the seams, who pays the debt? You?
I'll vote to leave when leaving costs less than staying. Not before.

ember.vell.yes.speaker: ember-vell
lines: The Sow's emptying. No figs, no bread, no fodder for the lift mules. Staying's costing more than going.
My vote is yes.

ember.vell.yesFire.speaker: ember-vell
lines: Look at it. Nobody's paying any debts to a mountain like that.
My vote is yes.

ember.bron.hello.speaker: ember-bron
lines: The guild says dig, we dig. The guild says stop, we stop.
It's not my place to say what the mountain's doing. It's my place to bring the shift up alive.

ember.bron.tithe.speaker: ember-bron
lines: What? You look like you've seen the bottom of the shaft.

options.text: Take Bron to see the cage.

ember.bron.shown.speaker: ember-bron
lines: Hal. Hal Tanner. They told us he went south.
Every name on this board went south.
We're bringing them up. Then we're leaving, and the guild can dig its own hole.

ember.bron.going.speaker: ember-bron
lines: Go on. We'll get the shift out. All of it, this time.

ember.wyn.hello.speaker: ember-wyn
lines: Mind the rails. The carts don't stop for ghosts.

ember.wyn.going.speaker: ember-wyn
lines: We're going. Debt and all.

ember.ifor.hello.speaker: ember-ifor
lines: Four seasons I owe Vell. Four seasons of the deep shift.
If the mountain wants to cancel that, I'll not argue with it.

ember.gethin.hello.speaker: ember-gethin
lines: I do the lamps. All of them. They never go out, not ever.

ember.cole.father.speaker: ember-cole
lines: Da! They brought him up. He's thin, and he can't see right in the light, but he's walking.
He says there were others down there with him. Bron's bringing them all.

ember.annick.hello.speaker: ember-annick
lines: You come up the mountain with a cold in you. We don't get many visitors who are dead.
If you have come to tell me the mountain is waking, I know. I have known for longer than you have had a shape.
And don't bring me your measurements. The mountain is not a cart to be weighed.

ember.annick.omens.speaker: ember-annick
lines: The signs are coming, one by one, as it was written.
It is not a warning. It is the calling. The last Shaper's hearth is inside this mountain, and it is waking for us.

ember.annick.alone.speaker: ember-annick
lines: So. You read them the end of the scripture. Go down, and do not look back.
They have gone down. I will not. I will be at the spring when it comes.

options.text: Promise to stand with her at the spring when it comes.

ember.annick.taken.speaker: ember-annick
lines: Put me down. Put me DOWN.
You will carry me off my own mountain? Then you are what the fen says you are.

ember.annick.forced.speaker: ember-annick
lines: (She will not look at you.)

ember.annick.promised.speaker: ember-annick
lines: ...Then you are a stranger thing than I thought.
At the spring, then. When the bell rings on its own.

ember.annick.promise.speaker: ember-annick
lines: You'll come back. I can see it on you. At the spring, when the bell rings on its own.

ember.edda.hello.speaker: ember-edda
lines: Welcome, cold one. The Seer reads the mountain. We tend the spring and ring the hours.
The scripture is on the stone by the door. Fifty lines. Most of us have never needed the last one.

ember.edda.seer.speaker: ember-edda
lines: The Seer says the signs are the calling. The Seer has never been wrong.

ember.edda.read.speaker: ember-edda
lines: You've seen the signs. I've seen them too. I've been waiting for someone to say it.

options.text: Read Nerys the end of the scripture: go down, children, and do not look back.

ember.edda.going.speaker: ember-edda
lines: Go down, and do not look back. I have said it a thousand times and never once listened to it.
We'll take the pilgrims' path round the north flank. It's ours. Nobody else knows it in the ash.
The Seer will not come. You know that.

ember.edda.gone.speaker: ember-edda
lines: Down, and not looking back.

ember.chapel.bells.speaker: ember-edda
lines: (A raised hand. The bell is ringing. No one here speaks while the bell speaks.)

ember.annick.bells.speaker: ember-annick
lines: (A raised hand. The bell is ringing. No one here speaks while the bell speaks.)

ember.corwen.hello.speaker: ember-corwen
lines: The cells are warm this year. Warmer every night. I've stopped needing a blanket.

ember.lio.hello.speaker: ember-lio
lines: Eleven years I've rung the hours. Lately the bell rings a little before I touch it. The ground shakes it.

ember.ysolt.hello.speaker: ember-ysolt
lines: Is it true there's green down there? Like in the stories?

ember.brannoc.hello.speaker: ember-brannoc
lines: Taste the spring, if you want. I won't stop you. I won't tell you what you'll find either.

ember.faithful.going.speaker: ember-corwen
lines: Down. Not looking back.

ember.aled.camp.lied.speaker: ember-aled
lines: You said that night. I spent it counting the flock and you knew the mountain would still be there at dawn.

ember.aled.camp.lost.speaker: ember-aled
lines: Bethan's cistern had water when ours ran dry. I've put a full jug by the road twice now.

ember.aled.camp.shown.speaker: ember-aled
lines: I can still see the ice go white on the trough and lift off it. The ewes put their noses down and turned away.

ember.aled.camp.rumour.speaker: ember-aled
lines: A boy from the mine brought up a sack of feed. He said his father's name was on the board they hung from the cage.

ember.aled.camp.home.speaker: ember-aled
lines: The two ewes in the pen are Nia's. I leave the gate bar low enough for her to reach.

ember.nia.camp.lied.speaker: ember-nia
lines: I slept in my boots that night. Grandad said I could take them off when it got light.

ember.nia.camp.lost.speaker: ember-nia
lines: I put a bowl down for Ffion's dog. A gull took what was in it.

ember.nia.camp.shown.speaker: ember-nia
lines: Grandad showed me where your ice was. The white part on the edge was gone before I got there.

ember.nia.camp.rumour.speaker: ember-nia
lines: Dai heard what you said about the night. He asked if I'd been scared. I said I was asleep.

ember.nia.camp.home.speaker: ember-nia
lines: The small ewe keeps putting her head through the sticks. I moved the grass where she could reach it.

ember.bethan.camp.lied.speaker: ember-bethan
lines: You could have said you didn't know the hour. I'd still have put the crock on the cart.

ember.bethan.camp.lost.speaker: ember-bethan
lines: I've got Huw's sieve. He lent it to me the week the cistern sank. It's hanging behind the cloth.

ember.bethan.camp.shown.speaker: ember-bethan
lines: You made me put my hand under the old waterline. There was clay where the plaster had been.

ember.bethan.camp.rumour.speaker: ember-bethan
lines: They weighed my figs every week. I wonder if they put a weight on the cage when there was a man in it.

ember.bethan.camp.home.speaker: ember-bethan
lines: I saved the good crock and a rake. Tomos is using the crock to soak figs for the ones with sore teeth.

ember.tomos.camp.lied.speaker: ember-tomos
lines: Mother made me turn the cart around three times to see if anyone else was coming. You could have told us what you knew.

ember.tomos.camp.lost.speaker: ember-tomos
lines: Aled mended that wheel with a peg from his gate. I can hear it knock once on every turn.

ember.tomos.camp.shown.speaker: ember-tomos
lines: After you took her to the cistern, Mother carried the empty jugs to the cart herself.

ember.tomos.camp.rumour.speaker: ember-tomos
lines: I used to leave the figs by the cage. No one said what the names on that board were for.

ember.tomos.camp.home.speaker: ember-tomos
lines: I set the fig boards on two stones. They'll do for a bench if the little ones sit in the middle.

ember.huw.camp.lied.speaker: ember-huw
lines: I left a week's grain on the floor because you gave me a night. I would have gone if you'd shown me the crack.

ember.huw.camp.lost.speaker: ember-huw
lines: Mari borrowed my flail and tied its split end with vine. It's outlasted the floor.

ember.huw.camp.shown.speaker: ember-huw
lines: The crack made steam on the side we'd swept. I kept looking for where it began.

ember.huw.camp.rumour.speaker: ember-huw
lines: I let the rumour stand a day. I wish I'd sent someone to the lower farms with the truth of it.

ember.huw.camp.home.speaker: ember-huw
lines: I brought the flail. This ground won't take threshing, but the handle is good ash.

ember.elin.camp.lied.speaker: ember-elin
lines: The bees had settled. If I'd known there was another morning, I'd have taken a hive.

ember.elin.camp.lost.speaker: ember-elin
lines: Ffion used to keep a jar ready for me when the comb was full. I've still got the last one.

ember.elin.camp.shown.speaker: ember-elin
lines: Huw scraped the flour from the split. It came up wet. He didn't sweep that side again.

ember.elin.camp.rumour.speaker: ember-elin
lines: Huw wanted to wait after word went round. I left the harness hung from the shafts.

ember.elin.camp.home.speaker: ember-elin
lines: I brought the wax. When the thread is dry, I'll mend the tear over the cart.

ember.ffion.camp.lied.speaker: ember-ffion
lines: It didn't go that night. The dog wouldn't cross the byre door the next morning either. We were staying gone.

ember.ffion.camp.lost.speaker: ember-ffion
lines: Gwil used to bring a bucket when the hens went off their water. I've left his by the rope line.

ember.ffion.camp.shown.speaker: ember-ffion
lines: You stood where the dog stopped. I hadn't thought to look at the dust down near the floor.

ember.ffion.camp.rumour.speaker: ember-ffion
lines: They said the night had come and gone. The byre was every bit as still in the morning.

ember.ffion.camp.home.speaker: ember-ffion
lines: I brought the feed tin. The hens that are left lay under the cart for shelter.

ember.dai.camp.lied.speaker: ember-dai
lines: I told the dog it would be all right when the sun came up. I didn't tell him to go home.

ember.dai.camp.lost.speaker: ember-dai
lines: Bethan used to put the soft figs aside for me. Tomos has brought a few, but they're the hard ones.

ember.dai.camp.shown.speaker: ember-dai
lines: After you showed Gran the hens, she called the dog and he didn't come until she stepped out.

ember.dai.camp.rumour.speaker: ember-dai
lines: The grown-ups were talking about the night again. I went to get the dog before they asked me.

ember.dai.camp.home.speaker: ember-dai
lines: The dog wants to sleep under the cart. Gran says the cart will still be there in the morning.

ember.gwil.camp.lied.speaker: ember-gwil
lines: I drew water at first light and it was still hot. You didn't need to name a night.

ember.gwil.camp.lost.speaker: ember-gwil
lines: Huw carried from our well every other day. I kept the smoother handle on his bucket.

ember.gwil.camp.shown.speaker: ember-gwil
lines: It steamed before you laid the bucket on the coping. The rope was warm right up to my hand.

ember.gwil.camp.rumour.speaker: ember-gwil
lines: Word went over the walls before I drew the first bucket. The water was still hot.

ember.gwil.camp.home.speaker: ember-gwil
lines: Sian saved the rope. We've cut the hot end off and hung the pot with what was left.

ember.sian.camp.lied.speaker: ember-sian
lines: I filled the buckets to leave that night. In the morning I tipped one out to make the cart lighter.

ember.sian.camp.lost.speaker: ember-sian
lines: Mari used to water the new vines with this bucket. There's a cut in the handle where she hung it.

ember.sian.camp.shown.speaker: ember-sian
lines: Father gave me the rope after you left. It was warm where he'd been holding it.

ember.sian.camp.rumour.speaker: ember-sian
lines: Tomos says there were names on the cage. I thought the names in a tally were the ones that paid.

ember.sian.camp.home.speaker: ember-sian
lines: I brought both buckets. The shallow one leaks, so the dog can have that.

ember.mari.camp.lied.speaker: ember-mari
lines: I left my knife in the ground when you said it would go that night. A knife is easy to find. Look at the hill.

ember.mari.camp.lost.speaker: ember-mari
lines: Gwil was going to bring the long rope down for the terraces. There's still a hook for it by the steps.

ember.mari.camp.shown.speaker: ember-mari
lines: I watched the frost lift right out of my grandmother's soil. The vine above it still looked green.

ember.mari.camp.rumour.speaker: ember-mari
lines: They wanted to count the nights. I counted the vines that felt warm at the root.

ember.mari.camp.home.speaker: ember-mari
lines: I've put the vine cuttings where the cloth drips. Two still have green under the bark.

ember.rhys.camp.lied.speaker: ember-rhys
lines: You gave us one night. I had time to pick up the wire, if I'd known when to stop winding it.

ember.rhys.camp.lost.speaker: ember-rhys
lines: Aled said he'd take the broken gate off its hinge on the way out. It's still up when I close my eyes.

ember.rhys.camp.shown.speaker: ember-rhys
lines: Mother said to pull up a stake after you showed her the frost. The end came out warm.

ember.rhys.camp.rumour.speaker: ember-rhys
lines: When the word got round, I kept the cart pointed down the road. Easier than turning it twice.

ember.rhys.camp.home.speaker: ember-rhys
lines: I saved a coil of wire from the top terrace. It'll keep the rope off the wet ground.

ember.aled.spared.speaker: ember-aled
lines: The lava stopped a field above the fold. I went up and put my hand on it. Warm, like a ewe's back.

ember.nia.spared.speaker: ember-nia
lines: Dad says the mountain held its breath. I think something held it for us.

ember.aled.camp.stopped.speaker: ember-aled
lines: The mountain's gone quiet. When the ash settles we'll walk the ewes back up. The fold may still be there.

ember.nia.camp.stopped.speaker: ember-nia
lines: Dad says we can go home soon. I want to see if the gate bar is still where I left it.

ember.bethan.spared.speaker: ember-bethan
lines: The cistern's cracked worse, but it's ours, and it's standing. I'll have it plastered before the rains.

ember.tomos.spared.speaker: ember-tomos
lines: Mam swept the ash off the step four times today. It keeps coming down. She keeps sweeping.

ember.bethan.camp.stopped.speaker: ember-bethan
lines: We'll go back when the road cools. I want to know if the crock I left was the one that cracked.

ember.tomos.camp.stopped.speaker: ember-tomos
lines: Mam's already packing. We only just unpacked.

ember.huw.spared.speaker: ember-huw
lines: Floor's under a finger of ash. Under the ash it's still the floor. We'll thresh on it this year.

ember.elin.spared.speaker: ember-elin
lines: We sat in the dark all night with the door shut. In the morning the mountain was quiet and the birds came back first.

ember.huw.camp.stopped.speaker: ember-huw
lines: Quiet up there now. I'll go and look at the floor before I tell Elin anything.

ember.elin.camp.stopped.speaker: ember-elin
lines: He says he's only going to look. He's taking the flail.

ember.ffion.spared.speaker: ember-ffion
lines: The hens laid this morning. Through all of that, they laid.

ember.dai.spared.speaker: ember-dai
lines: The dog won't go up the lane past the black edge. I don't blame him. I don't go either.

ember.ffion.camp.stopped.speaker: ember-ffion
lines: The hens can go back first. They never wanted to come.

ember.dai.camp.stopped.speaker: ember-dai
lines: The mountain stopped. Mam says something stopped it. She won't say what.

ember.gwil.spared.speaker: ember-gwil
lines: The water's running clean again. Hot for a day, then clean. The well knew before we did.

ember.sian.spared.speaker: ember-sian
lines: Da won't say he was frightened. He drew water all night so he'd have something to do with his hands.

ember.gwil.camp.stopped.speaker: ember-gwil
lines: If the well's clean we go back. If it's not, we dig another. Either way we go back.

ember.sian.camp.stopped.speaker: ember-sian
lines: Da's been looking up the valley all morning. He doesn't say anything. He just looks.

ember.mari.spared.speaker: ember-mari
lines: The top terrace is under it. The bottom three stand. My grandmother set those vines; they'll set again.

ember.rhys.spared.speaker: ember-rhys
lines: Mam's taking cuttings from the burnt rows anyway. She says roots remember.

ember.mari.camp.stopped.speaker: ember-mari
lines: The cuttings can go back in the ground they came from. That's better than a row under a tarp.

ember.rhys.camp.stopped.speaker: ember-rhys
lines: It's quiet. You can hear the sea now, without the mountain over it.

ember.orrin.spared.speaker: ember-orrin
lines: The guild kept the town, and the mountain let it be kept. Don't ask me which of us to thank. I've stopped asking.

ember.annick.spared.speaker: ember-annick
lines: The bell stopped ringing on its own. We stood at the door all night and nothing came. I don't know what you did up there. I know you did something.

ember.cole.stopped.speaker: ember-cole
lines: I went up the road this morning. The lava's black right across it, and cold enough to stand on. It just stops. Like something told it to.

quests.title: The Mountain Is Waking
quests.summary: A miner's boy says the mountain is waking. The people who live on it have no reason to believe a hooded thing from the north.

steps.journal: A boy waits at the Cinder Shrine, below the cone's west side, watching the mountain.
Cole says there is new steam on the cone's north-west flank, high above the scree. Go and see what the ground is hiding.
Six farms in the green valley west of the cone: the Sow. They won't believe the mountain. Find what is wrong on each family's own land, and show the elder.

quests.title: The Guild of Cinderhold
quests.summary: The miners live by the guild’s word, and the guild lives by the mine.

steps.journal: Cinderhold, the miners' town on a bench of the cone's west flank, above the Sow. Three masters of the guild decide for everyone. Speak to Morcant, its head, in the hall.
The guild votes, two of three. Teg trusts numbers. Vell trusts money. Morcant trusts no one. The miners trust the guild.

quests.title: The Seer of the Ash Chapel
quests.summary: The pilgrims on the south flank live nearest the crater of anyone, and read the mountain by their own scripture.

steps.journal: The Ash Chapel, high on the cone's south-west flank, nearest the crater of anyone. Speak to Annick, its Seer.
The faithful believe their scripture, not measurements. It names three omens. Find them on the mountain, and wait for the bell before you speak.

ember-clue-bethan.name: The cistern
ember-clue-bethan.title: The cistern
ember-clue-bethan.text: A dark band runs round the plaster a hand above the water: last night's level. Along it, a hairline crack, and the plaster is warm to the touch.

ember-clue-huw.name: The threshing floor
ember-clue-huw.title: The threshing floor
ember-clue-huw.text: A crack runs across the flags, new and clean-edged. Warm air breathes up out of it, smelling of struck flint.

ember-clue-ffion.name: The byre
ember-clue-ffion.title: The byre
ember-clue-ffion.text: The air inside is still and heavy. Two hens lie on the floor with nothing on them. Near the ground, it's hard to breathe.

ember-clue-thermo.name: The bell-thermometer
ember-clue-thermo.title: The bell in the deep seam
ember-clue-thermo.text: An iron rod runs down into the seam; the glass bell on top of it is fogged and hot to the touch. The bead inside stands above every mark on the guild's board. The highest mark is a hand's width below it.

ember-clue-cage.name: The cage
ember-clue-cage.title: The tithe cage
ember-clue-cage.text: A board is nailed inside the cage: names, chalked and struck through, a tally of seasons by each. Debts. The newest name is fresh: HAL TANNER. Cole's father. The guild told the town its debtors went south.

ember-clue-scripture.name: The scripture
ember-clue-scripture.title: The scripture stone
ember-clue-scripture.text: Fifty lines, carved deep and worn shallow. The last ones are clean, as if no one's hand has ever rested there: "When the spring sours, when the birds fall out of the air, when the mountain breathes by day, the hearth is calling. Go down, children, and do not look back."

ember-clue-birds.name: The still hollow
ember-clue-birds.title: The still hollow
ember-clue-birds.text: Birds lie on the ash with nothing on them, wings folded as if they landed to sleep. Your cowl light gutters; the air here is heavy and does not move. You take one, light in the hand.
